what: M6b flame spread predictor: spread rate with range, will-it-spread verdict, calibration label and in-domain flag, by material, flow direction, flow speed and O2, at 1 atm, microgravity only.
layout: every 2-D array is [o2 index][flow index]; null = no data and no model
verdict_meaning: observed no-spread / near observed extinction: inside the boxes of RULES.md section 4 around an observed NASA no-spread case of the same material, flow direction and geometry. 'spreads' only means no such case is near; it is not a claim that the fuel is flammable or that anything is safe.

cases.fuel: PMMA film 0.1 mm, both faces burning
cases.note: de Ris x thin-regime factor fitted on 1-2 mm slabs; films are thinner than any calibration row, so every cell is out of domain. Independent check on a 100 um film: see models/m6b-predictor/REPORT.md.

cases.fuel: PMMA slab 1 mm, both faces burning
cases.note: Thick-regime cells: observed bound from PSI-99 (thick PMMA anchored: 0 to 0.167 mm/s), in domain only near 20 cm/s and 22% O2. Thin-regime cells: no data (null).

Concurrent scaling law (rate proportional to flow x O2 x sqrt(pressure) / area density) x one constant fitted on six reported spacecraft flights; checked on Saffire-II (PSI-99).

limits: Reduced-order model calibrated to NASA ISS and spacecraft data; not validated fluid dynamics. Microgravity only: no Moon or Mars prediction. Outside the in-domain cells every value is an extrapolation. Nothing here says a material or atmosphere is safe.
